Choose a fixed \(A\in(0,\tfrac12]\), say \(A=\tfrac12\), and treat the two conjuncts separately.

For the zeta bound, use a truncated Dirichlet-series/Euler–Maclaurin representation of \(\zeta(s)\) with truncation height \(N\asymp |t|\). If
\[
\sigma\ge 1-\frac{A}{\log |t|},
\]
then \(N^{1-\sigma}\le e^A\), so the truncated sum is bounded by \(O_A(\log |t|)\); the correction and remainder terms are uniformly smaller when \(|t|>3\). This yields a constant \(C>0\) such that
\[
|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le C\log |t|
\]
throughout the stated strip.

For \(\psi(x)\sim x\), follow the standard analytic proof of the prime number theorem: prove that \(\zeta\) has no zeros on \(\Re s=1\), use
\[
-\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}
  =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^s},
\]
and apply a Tauberian theorem (or Perron inversion with contour displacement) to the simple pole at \(s=1\). Useful intermediate goals are therefore the uniform truncated-series estimate, nonvanishing of \(\zeta\) on \(\Re s=1\), and the identification of the logarithmic derivative’s coefficients with the von Mangoldt function.
